spec.description: AngelStep acoustic underlays from Acoustica Pty Ltd provide maximum impact noise control and sound absorption for residential and commercial developments, achieving up to a 6-star acoustic rating.
features: Unique patented technology combining sound absorber with impact and vibration damping
Available in various variations for different flooring substrates
Achieves up to the highest 6-star acoustic rating
Includes instructions for various floor finishes
install: Level structural floor to parquetry installation standard tolerances
Fill gaps and holes in floor
Install 40mm x (AS thickness -1mm) MDF battens around the perimeter
Leave 3mm gap between walls and finish surface
Spot glue AngelStep with Maxibond or equal
Install skirting after floor with 2 to 3mm gap

NOTE :	THE NATIONAL OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY COMMISSION PRODUCED IN AUGUST 1988 A CODE OF PRACTICE AND GUIDANCE NOTES ON ASBESTOS.  IN THE PREFACE TO THAT DOCUMENT, PART 3, Clause 3.1, second paragraph states :
“ASBESTOS REMOVAL MAY NOT BE IMMEDIATELY NECESSARY, BUT MUST BE COMPLETED BEFORE A STRUCTURE OR PART OF A STRUCTURE IS DEMOLISHED.”
General
A.	Scope
The work of this section includes but is not limited to the following items:
Supply and installation of AngelStep floor system. 
Acoustica’s best performing flooring underlay range, AngelStep is the top choice for discerning residential and commercial developments where maximum impact noise control and sound absorption is needed.
Available in different variations to suit flooring substrates and materials, AngelStep features unique patented technology that combines a sound absorber with impact and vibration damping to consistently achieve up to the highest 6-star acoustic rating dependent on installation. 
B.	Examine documents:  Examine parts of the drawings and this specification for requirements which affect the work of this specification.  In particular, take note of other trades involved along with relevant body corporate requirements and/or criterions outlined in the strata by-laws i.e. AAAC star rating.
The NCC provides minimum construction standards for
various building classes including acoustic privacy. The NCC
requirement is a weighted standardised impact sound
pressure level with spectrum adaptation term Ci, of less than
or equal to 62 Lnt,W+Ci. However, the reality is that this is in
most cases unacceptable to occupants and can result in the
need for costly reparation works. In response, the Association
of Australian Acoustic Consultants (AAAC) has developed the
star rating system to rank the acoustical quality of
apartments and provide guidance in the design and
construction process.
